You Paid Into Social Security for 40 Years. Then This.
youtube_short.description: You paid into Social Security from every paycheck for 40 straight years — and when you finally collect, the IRS can tax up to 85% of your benefits. Congress set the income thresholds in 1983 at $34,000 for singles and never adjusted them for inflation. What started as a tax on 10% of recipients now hits 56% — not because anything changed, but because inflation quietly dragged everyone over the line. The average affected retiree pays $4,200 extra a year, adding up to $84,000 over a 20-year retirement on money already taxed once. The fix is Roth conversions in your fifties before you claim — subscribe so you don't miss more moves like this. #socialsecurity #retirement #taxes #personalfinance
